summary: Iteration 17 — Live HUD workout-driven target power. Backend 7/7 pytest PASSED (new suite /app/backend/tests/test_ws_live_hud.py): WS /api/ws/telemetry 'init' resets elapsed to <7s and hovers power near supplied watts (180→avg ~180±8W); 'target' 320W drives streamed power to avg 305–335W within a few seconds; 'erg', 'pause', 'resume', 'dropout' all still work (paused elapsed growth ≤ resumed growth; dropout stops frames then recovers). GET /api/progress returns FTP metric '287 W' (used by Settings auto-sync). POST /api/coach/cue accepts the new optional 'segment' and 'zone' fields and returns a 200 cue with EMERGENT_LLM_KEY set. Frontend (landscape tablet 1280x800) — /workout?workoutId=vo2-max-intervals renders WITHOUT the hardcoded 251 W: POWER TARGET 187 W, ZONE Z2, STEP 1/13, TIME LEFT 8:20, NEXT UP 'Tempo Block · 6:43 · 230 W · RPE 5'; workout title 'VO2 Max Intervals'; interval profile bars highlight the active warm-up bar; elapsed starts near 0. Confirmed workout-specific differences: endurance-ride → STEP 1/3, NEXT UP 'Tempo Block · 81:54 · 230 W'; recovery-spin → STEP 1/3, NEXT UP 'Endurance · 31:12 · 187 W'. Distinct step counts (13 vs 3 vs 3) and distinct NEXT UP labels/durations prove it is driven by the chosen workout's segments, not static. Settings POWER PROFILE card shows current FTP with +/- steppers correctly DISABLED while 'Auto-update from training progress' is ON, enabled when OFF (verified by +5 → 292 W then -5 → 287 W). Rider Profile FTP stat updates in real time (287 → 292 → 287). W/kg stat is derived from FTP.

Not a functional bug but breaks tests that select by [data-testid="profile"]. Consider renaming the profile Card to testID='rider-profile'. Reference: /app/frontend/app/settings.tsx:67

action_items: Optional: rename Settings profile card testID from 'profile' to 'rider-profile' to avoid Playwright strict-mode conflict with any duplicate 'profile' locator on the page.
Optional: migrate deprecated 'textShadow*' style props to 'textShadow' object and move pointerEvents from prop to style to silence RN Web warnings on /workout.
critical_code_review_comments: workout.tsx line 172: sendInit is dispatched once (initSent ref) and subsequent segment changes only call sendTarget — correct so elapsed is not repeatedly reset while the ride is in progress.

workout-catalog.ts buildSegments always begins with a Z2 warm-up (mkSeg(w,1,...)) so all workouts open at 0.65 × FTP; that's why VO2, Endurance and Recovery all show 187 W target on step 1 (287 × 0.65 ≈ 187). Differentiation kicks in on subsequent segments — confirmed via NEXT UP.
settings.ts fetchProgressFtp() parses digits from the FTP metric value ('287 W') — resilient to unit label. AsyncStorage write is fire-and-forget with .catch() no-op which is fine.
server.py TrainerSim.step uses base_target directly with ±8 W jitter — 'target' message therefore takes effect on the next 200 ms tick (verified in test).
seed_data_creation: None. Coach cue POST used a transient payload; no DB writes required for the new WS/init/target/progress flows.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The Live HUD is now fully driven by workout-catalog.ts segments and FTP from settings. Every workout starts with a Z2 warm-up so step 1 will always show 187 W target when FTP=287. To see distinct targets, either wait for the segment to advance or hit /workout?workoutId=... and read STEP count + NEXT UP (both differ per workout). Settings Power Profile ftp-minus/ftp-plus are disabled via the disabled prop when settings.ftpAuto=true (visually dimmed s.ftpBtnOff style). WS test: use websockets>=13 sync client, drain the initial {type:'status'} frame, wait ~2s after sending 'target' so any buffered frames from the previous target flush before sampling. Backend base URL: EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_ws_live_hud.py can be re-run standalone.
rca_of_issue: No new bugs. During test construction, the 'target' assertion initially failed because buffered telemetry frames from before the target change polluted the tail sample; fix: drain the socket for ~3s after sending the target message before sampling. Not a product bug — verifies the trainer sim responds within one tick as designed.
